entities.name: the 汴河 at the moorings
entities.what: The 汴河's westernmost reach in S4b: a basin of open water left as plain silk with small scattered ripple ticks and a few swirl eddies near the bank, holding five boats moored side by side with their west ends at the bank and a sixth along the far bank at the top; it opens east toward the Rainbow Bridge (S3).
entities.vis: part: boats cover most of it; the far shore is behind the small cabin boat; willow whips and roofs cover the south shore east of u 15050
entities.note: No shoreline is inked. shore_s (the near bank, south and west of the water) is read where the bank's dark wash streaks stop and the ripple ticks and swirls begin: the landing in front of the top-left building (v 203-242 at u 14860-15025), along the boats' west ends (hidden behind the long-cabin boat's west end, est), the first ripples at (14778, 455), swirls at u 14768-14808 v 617-672 round the mooring post (14738, 662), then the dark edge band running SE (14900, 778)-(15040, 862) with ripples above it at u 15025-15110 v 815-850; east of 15050 it runs along the back of a roof and under willow whips (est, v 875-896). shore_n (the far bank, north) is hidden behind the small cabin boat (hull v 77-160): est v 112-122, south of the far bank's top at v ~80. THE WEST END: the strip u 15030-15180, v 85-150 between the top-left building and the far bank is read as land (a landing; faint wash, no ripple ticks; the restyle paints sand there), so in S4b the water does not reach the silk's top edge (conf low). Other reading: it is the far bank's south face (top v ~81 = the shed's ground line, foot v ~150 = a faint stroke at u 15050-15103), and the water reaches up to it. SEAM u 15500: shore_s v ~896 (est, under willow whips), shore_n v ~112 (est); both run on east into S3 (S3's near shore lies at about v 900-1000 by 十千脚店, its far bank at the top). The restyle paints the water as a pale sheet; nothing here is taken from its colour edge.

entities.name: near bank of the moorings
entities.what: The low sandy bank on the town side of the moorings: a landing in front of the top-left building, then the bank where the bank path meets the boats' west ends (a gangplank runs from it to the mat-cargo boat), a mooring post at the water's edge, and the edge behind the riverside roofs and willows to the east; washed with dark streaks, no revetment, stair or jetty.
entities.vis: part: boats' ends, roofs and willows cover it
entities.note: bank_top is where the flat ground ends: the foot of the top-left building's front wall runs (14900, 170)-(15030, 142) and the landing in front of it is open to v ~200; the bank path's figures (t4) stand at v ~403 at u 14640-14800; south of the mooring post the top is hidden under the tea house's and the riverside building's roofs (est). The slope between bank_top and shore is narrow in the picture (45-70 px of v), drawn with diagonal ink-wash streaks, no vertical face. Bank top taken at street level (H 0): it is the same open ground as the top street. A small stippled tree or heap stands on the bank at u 14795-14840 v 222-345 (t4's). MERGE: the stippled small tree or heap on the bank is S4b.tree.stump_14805 (added in the merge). FRAME: its shore line stands on the support `water` (support_by), like S4b.water.bian_river's shores; its bank_top on the ground (street level).

entities.name: far bank of the river at the top edge
entities.what: The river's far (north) bank along the silk's top edge: a long open shed on posts at its west end and a row of bare willows with drooping whips, faintly drawn, their feet at about v 75-80; the small cabin boat lies along it.
entities.vis: part: cut by the silk's top edge at v ~15; the small cabin boat hides its foot
entities.note: bank_top = the shed's ground line (posts' feet at u 15040-15160, v 75-85) running on east under the willow trunks (feet at about (15230, 62), (15305, 75), (15520, 70), est). The bank's face toward the water is hidden by the small cabin boat. The restyle paints a far shore here with a tiled house at u 15100-15190 (the scan's shed) and two leafed willows; the trees are bare in the scan. The shed and the willows are land things (left to structures_e and t5). FRAME: its shore line stands on the support `water` (support_by), like S4b.water.bian_river's shores; its bank_top on the ground (street level).

entities.name: mooring post at the water's edge
entities.what: A short post with a rounded knob at the water's edge, where the bank meets the river below the bank path; two ropes from the big cabin boat's west end are tied to it, and a long pole lies from its foot along the boat.
entities.note: Knob u 14727-14743, v 645-660; ripples and swirls round it at u 14750-14817 v 613-672, so it stands in the water's edge (the river agent's prop). The restyle draws the knob as the end of the long pole; the scan shows the ropes looping round it. FRAME: support `ground` -> `water`: its foot (14737, 665, est) is on the shore point (14738, 662), in the water's edge, so it stands at the water level.

entities.name: big cabin boat (the biggest moored boat)
entities.what: The biggest boat of the moorings, the southernmost of five moored side by side with their west ends to the bank: a long timber hull with planked strakes and nail rows; at the west (bank) end a raked end under a hip-roofed cabin with a man seated on its roof; a long cabin with planked walls and posts along the middle, round woven baskets or bales on deck (u 15190-15360, v 600-700), a mat-roofed after cabin with railings (u 15500-15805) and a long tapering sweep blade trailing east in the water beyond the stern (u 15680-15855). A long spar lies along the cabin tops (v 625-640) from u ~15150 to a brush-like end at u ~15865: probably the lowered mast (a short post at u ~15340, v 575-620 may be its tabernacle; conf low). Two ropes run from the west end to S4b.prop.mooring_post_14737; a long pole lies from the post's foot along the hull's south side to about (15200, 765); another pole leans through a rope loop on the south side at (15440, 820) with its lower end in the water at (15343, 880). Rafted to S4b.veh.boat_arched_awning_14945 on its north side.
entities.vis: part: willow branches cross its east half; the rafted boats hide its north side
entities.note: ORIENTATION (both readings): the boats' bank ends are read as bows and their outer (east) ends as sterns, because the outer ends carry what marks a stern: the round boat's transom with a rudder stock (S4b.veh.boat_round_mat_15025), a vertical stock and a sweep pole at the arched-awning boat's east end, a long tapering sweep blade trailing in the water beyond the big boat's east end, the small boat's cabin and tiller at its east end. The lead's first look read sterns to the bank (retired at the merge). SCALE CUE: hull u 14903-15855 (about 950 px along u including the sweep; 12.3 m between the front and rear waterline points at painted size with the seed frame); freeboard (gunwale with nail row to the near-side waterline) 57 px at u 15200 (773 -> 830), 55 at u 15300 (790 -> 845), 47 at u 15400; the middle cabin's walls about 100 px from eave to deck at the west end (posts u 14972-15010, v ~600-700). Waterline evidence: the darkest bottom strake on the near side, (15000, 767), (15100, 797), (15200, 830), (15300, 845); water ripples below it at u 15025-15250, v 815-886. The west end's foot (14928, 703) is the bottom of the raked end. EAST END PAST THE SEAM: the after cabin's mat roof runs u 15500-15805 (eave tip (15805, 685)), railings and posts at u 15640-15760 v 760-850, the sweep blade (15690, 850)-(15855, 897), the spar's end (15830-15865, 630-650): Phase 0 gives the whole boat to S4b although its east end lies in S3's range (the lead's look put the bow at ≈15450). Lines: ropes from (14895-14927, 627-647) to the post's knob; the long pole two lines about 5 px apart from (14740, 660) through (14900, 712) to about (15200, 765), where it meets the deck edge (a gangplank or a pole laid along the hull; conf low). MERGE (the lead's rule, 2026-10-12: the end with the rudder or the sweep is the stern): settled as recorded, front at the bank (west) end and rear at the outer (east) end with the stern gear; the "sterns to the bank" reading is retired, so front/rear and facing_deg stay as they are. MERGE (the lead's note on this boat): the part already runs to the true stern, so nothing is extended: rear is the stern's foot (15745, 865, est) under the raked end (15760, 777), with the after cabin to u 15805 and the sweep blade to (15855, 897) as part of the boat (merge agent's overlay, scratchpad S4b_merge/ov_bigboat_east.jpg). S3's t1 agent read a "bow at about (15790, 670-755)": that is this after cabin's eave tip (15805, 685) over the stern. S3's river_w does not record this boat.

entities.name: boat with an arched mat awning
entities.what: A boat moored between the mat-cargo boat and the big cabin boat, its west end hidden behind the big boat's roof cabin: an arched mat awning on hoops over its after half (u 15105-15407, v 459-560), a boatman seated under the awning's east end, a dark upturned head at the east end, a vertical stock (rudder?) and a pole slanting into the water below him; a rope from the east end runs east-south-east into the open water and ends with a small splash mark at (15592, 584) (an anchor line, past the seam). Rafted between S4b.veh.boat_mat_cargo_14900 (north) and S4b.veh.boat_big_cabin_14928 (south).
entities.vis: part: west half hidden behind the big cabin boat's roof cabin and its seated man
entities.note: ORIENTATION (both readings): the boats' bank ends are read as bows and their outer (east) ends as sterns, because the outer ends carry what marks a stern: the round boat's transom with a rudder stock (S4b.veh.boat_round_mat_15025), a vertical stock and a sweep pole at the arched-awning boat's east end, a long tapering sweep blade trailing in the water beyond the big boat's east end, the small boat's cabin and tiller at its east end. The lead's first look read sterns to the bank (retired at the merge). The lead's first look counted four rafted boats and missed this one (it lies under the mat-cargo boat's bow and over the big boat's long cabin). SCALE CUE: awning u 15105-15407 (300 px), its east end v 495-505; the hull's east end curves down from (15395, 535) to the waterline behind the big boat's top rail at about v 600; freeboard at the east end about 65 px (deck v ~535 -> waterline ~600). The west end (front) is not painted: taken at the bank line with the others (est), anywhere from u 14900 to 15100. MERGE (the lead's rule, 2026-10-12: the end with the rudder or the sweep is the stern): settled as recorded, front at the bank (west) end and rear at the outer (east) end with the stern gear; the "sterns to the bank" reading is retired, so front/rear and facing_deg stay as they are.

entities.name: boat with mat-covered cargo
entities.what: A long boat moored with its west end near the bank: a dark barrel-shaped mat roof over its west end (u 14905-15020, v 400-470), a deck loaded with woven mats or matted bales along the middle (u 15020-15275), a row of round coils or flat baskets on its deck at u 15040-15160 v 420-460, and a long tapering hatched spar projecting east at deck level to a point at (15390, 458) (a raised sweep, or a pointed bow board). A gangplank (a straight board about 4 px wide) runs from the bank path at (14760, 402), where t4's porter with two baskets stands, down to its west end at (14895, 463). A rope with small loops runs from about (15335, 468) east into the water, ending at (15507, 511) (an anchor line). Rafted between S4b.veh.boat_long_cabin_14850 (north) and S4b.veh.boat_arched_awning_14945 (south).
entities.vis: part: the boats north and south of it hide both waterlines
entities.note: ORIENTATION (both readings): the boats' bank ends are read as bows and their outer (east) ends as sterns, because the outer ends carry what marks a stern: the round boat's transom with a rudder stock (S4b.veh.boat_round_mat_15025), a vertical stock and a sweep pole at the arched-awning boat's east end, a long tapering sweep blade trailing in the water beyond the big boat's east end, the small boat's cabin and tiller at its east end. The lead's first look read sterns to the bank (retired at the merge). This is the setup agent's fifth hull (v ~340-440 at its middle). SCALE CUE: hull u 14882-15390 (about 510 px); the west end rises from its foot (14900, 505, est) to (14888, 398); the gangplank's foot on the bank is the porter's path, its far end the boat's west end. The east waterline is hidden under the arched-awning boat's roof (est). MERGE (the lead's rule, 2026-10-12: the end with the rudder or the sweep is the stern): settled as recorded, front at the bank (west) end and rear at the outer (east) end with the stern gear; the "sterns to the bank" reading is retired, so front/rear and facing_deg stay as they are.

entities.name: long boat with a deckhouse

Rafted between S4b.veh.boat_round_mat_15025 (north, whose stern rests over its middle) and S4b.veh.boat_mat_cargo_14900 (south).
entities.vis: part: the mat-cargo boat hides its south waterline, the round boat its middle

entities.name: round-sterned boat with a barrel mat roof
entities.what: A broad boat moored at the top of the group, seen almost end-on: its pointed bow with a forked post touches the landing at the top-left (forked post top (15012, 168)), its broad stern faces the viewer and the river to the south-east: a squared transom with an arched opening and a rudder stock (u 15155-15175, v 255-295) between bulging hull sides (u 15017-15252), a big arched mat roof over the hull (u 15045-15200, v 160-230); two poles lie over the bow, from (14965, 175) to (15015, 222) and at (14990-15020, 235-255). Its stern rests over the middle of S4b.veh.boat_long_cabin_14850.
entities.vis: part: end-on, the bow foreshortened behind the roof
entities.note: Not one of the side-by-side row: it lies bow-in at an angle (heading about 148°, north-west), its stern over the long boat. SCALE CUE: beam 235 px across the bulging sides at v ~270 (u 15017-15252), transom about 80 px wide (15120-15200), roof top v 160; the hull's length is foreshortened (about 150 px from the forked post to the transom). The rudder end is read as the stern (the restyle reads it the same way); the forked post may be a bow bitt. rear = the transom's foot at the rudder; front est under the forked post. MERGE (the lead's rule, 2026-10-12: the end with the rudder is the stern): settled as recorded, rear at the transom with the rudder stock.

entities.name: small cabin boat by the far bank
entities.what: A smaller boat moored along the river's far bank at the top of the silk, lying east-west: an up-swept pointed west end with a small post or flag on it (15208-15218, 75-83), a low mat canopy over its west half, a higher mat-roofed cabin at its east end (u 15330-15460, v 62-90) with an opening in its end wall, and a short stick projecting east at deck level (u 15460-15487, v 83-90; a tiller?). No mast, no crew.
entities.note: Both ends are west of the seam (hull u 15177-15460, the stick to 15487), so it is S4b's. The restyle lengthens it to u ≈ 15520 and adds a mast and a crewman on the cabin roof (u 15330-15370, v 40-90): the scan has willow trunks of the far bank there (u 15297-15387, v 17-75), no mast and no figure. Bow at the up-swept west end, stern at the cabin (conf low; the other reading turns it by 180). SCALE CUE: hull 280 px long, gunwale to waterline about 55-65 px at the west end (92 -> 158), near-side waterline (15200, 150), (15300, 153), (15367, 147), rising to (15417, 133) at the east end. MERGE (the lead's rule, 2026-10-12: the end with the rudder is the stern): the tiller-like stick at the east end marks the stern, so the recorded bow (the up-swept west end) stands.
